SELECTED_INDEX: 4
CONFIDENCE: 0.70
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows an intense aromatic ring breathing band at ~999 cm⁻¹ (typical for monosubstituted benzenes), strong aromatic C=C stretches at 1589/1602 cm⁻¹, and clear aliphatic/aromatic C–H stretching bands in the 2900–3100 cm⁻¹ region (GFQ-003). A prominent band at 1247 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of an aryl–O–alkyl ether (anisole-type) C–O stretch, supporting an Ar–O–R structure. The presence of a CH₃ group is indicated by the 1458 cm⁻¹ bending band (GFQ-003), and a band near 619 cm⁻¹ is consistent with an aliphatic C–Cl stretch (in the general halogen stretch region; cf. halogen-related frequencies around ~600–700 cm⁻¹ noted in GFQ-040/046 for inorganic analogs). Together, these features best match CC(Cl)COc1ccccc1 (an aryl ether with a secondary carbon-bound Cl and a CH₃ group), over the ethoxy chloride (1, lacking CH₃) or aryl-chloride/benzyl alcohol variants (7, 8, lacking the anisole-like 1247 cm⁻¹ ether band).
